title: Replace grid layout with Sugiyama DAG layout
postconditions: calculate_grid_layout in diagram_tool/src/layout/grid.rs is REPLACED by a new function dag_layout(doc: &DiagramDocument, settings: &DagLayoutSettings) -> DiagramDocument
The new layout respects edge topology: nodes connected by edges are positioned in layers
Locked nodes are not moved (same contract as grid layout)
Child nodes (node.parent.is_some()) move with their parent by the same delta
Toolbar 'Auto-Arrange' button calls dag_layout instead of calculate_grid_layout
All existing layout tests still pass or are updated to reflect new topology-aware behavior
invariants: If the graph has cycles, fall back silently to grid layout — never panic
Pure function: input DiagramDocument is not mutated, returns new DiagramDocument
Positions stored as OrderedFloat(f64), not f32
implementation_notes: SOURCE to port: graph/layout.rs DagLayout::apply() — this is the Sugiyama implementation with petgraph toposort + barycenter crossing minimization
ADAPTOR needed: graph/layout.rs works on Vec<Node> with f32 x/y and Vec<Connection>. diagram_tool works on im::HashMap<NodeId,Node> with OrderedFloat(f64) and im::HashMap<EdgeId,Edge>

STEPS: (1) Add petgraph = '0.8' to diagram_tool/Cargo.toml under [dependencies], (2) Create diagram_tool/src/layout/dag.rs with the ported DagLayout, (3) Adapt types at boundary: collect im::HashMap into petgraph graph, run layout, write positions back as OrderedFloat, (4) Replace call site in toolbar.rs
DO NOT import anything from the root graph/ crate — copy and adapt the algorithm inline
test_plan: GIVEN a document with 3 nodes A->B->C connected in sequence WHEN dag_layout is called THEN node X positions increase left to right (A.x < B.x < C.x)
GIVEN a document with no edges WHEN dag_layout is called THEN nodes are arranged in a grid (same as current behavior)
GIVEN a document with a cycle A->B->A WHEN dag_layout is called THEN function returns a valid DiagramDocument without panicking
GIVEN a document with locked nodes WHEN dag_layout is called THEN locked node positions are unchanged
GIVEN the same document applied twice WHEN dag_layout is called THEN positions are identical (deterministic)

title: Replace straight SVG lines with smooth bezier step edges
preconditions: canvas.rs SVG layer uses <line> elements for edges
postconditions: All edges in the SVG layer render as smooth-step bezier paths using <path> elements
Edge arrowhead markers are defined in the SVG <defs> section and applied to directed edges
The temporary edge drawn during DrawingEdge interaction mode also uses the smooth-step path
invariants: Pure math function: create_smooth_step_path(from: (f64,f64), to: (f64,f64)) -> String returns an SVG path string
implementation_notes: SOURCE: busted-flow/DIOXUS_PORT_REFERENCE.rs function create_smooth_step_path() — this is 15 lines of pure geometry already expressed in Rust
LOCATION: Add the function to diagram_tool/src/ui/canvas.rs or extract to diagram_tool/src/ui/edge_path.rs
REPLACE: The existing SVG <line> rendering block in canvas.rs (approximately lines 262-273) — replace <line> with <path d=smooth_step_path ... />
ARROWHEAD: Add an SVG <defs> block with a <marker id='arrow'> triangle. Apply marker-end='url(#arrow)' to directed edges (edge.directed == true)
TEMPORARY EDGE: The DrawingEdge SVG line (approx lines 283-286) also gets the smooth-step treatment
test_plan: GIVEN two nodes at (0,0) and (200,100) WHEN create_smooth_step_path is called THEN the result starts with 'M 0 0' and ends with 'L 200 100'
GIVEN two nodes at the same X position (dx < 2) WHEN create_smooth_step_path is called THEN result is a straight vertical line 'M x y L x y2'
GIVEN a directed edge WHEN rendered THEN the SVG path element has marker-end attribute set
GIVEN an undirected edge WHEN rendered THEN no marker-end attribute is present

title: Add rich ValidationIssue panel wired to schema validation
postconditions: A new ValidationPanel component exists at diagram_tool/src/ui/validation_panel.rs
ValidationPanel is mounted in app.rs alongside Canvas, visible below or beside PropertiesPanel
validate_schema() is called reactively when doc_signal changes (use_memo or use_effect)
ValidationIssue structs are displayed: each issue shows severity (Error/Warning), a short message, and which node or edge ID is affected
Toolbar gains a 'Validate' button that forces a re-validation run
Zero issues → panel shows a green 'Valid' indicator
One or more issues → panel shows a red count badge and lists each issue
invariants: validate_schema is a pure function — it receives &DiagramDocument and returns a Vec<ValidationIssue>
ValidationIssue is defined in diagram_tool/src/models/validation.rs (new file) — do NOT import from root graph/
ValidationPanel never panics if the issue list is empty
ValidationPanel is read-only — it does not mutate doc_signal
implementation_notes: DO NOT import graph::validation from the root crate. Instead, create diagram_tool/src/models/validation.rs that re-implements the relevant checks for DiagramDocument's type system (im::HashMap<NodeId,Node>, im::HashMap<EdgeId,Edge>)
Checks to implement: (1) edge source/target must exist in nodes map, (2) node.parent must exist and be NodeKind::Subgraph, (3) DAG cycle detection using existing validate_dag() from models/dag.rs
ValidationSeverity enum: Error | Warning
ValidationIssue struct: { severity: ValidationSeverity, code: &'static str, message: String, subject: Option<String> }
Reactive wiring: in app.rs, use use_memo(move || { validate_schema(&doc_signal.read()) }) and pass result down to ValidationPanel as a prop
test_plan: GIVEN a document with an edge pointing to a non-existent node WHEN validate_schema is called THEN result contains a ValidationIssue with severity Error and code 'edge-dangling'
GIVEN a document with a cycle A->B->A WHEN validate_schema is called THEN result contains a ValidationIssue with code 'dag-cycle'
GIVEN a node with parent set to a non-Subgraph node WHEN validate_schema is called THEN result contains ValidationIssue with code 'invalid-parent'
GIVEN a valid document with no issues WHEN validate_schema is called THEN result is an empty Vec
GIVEN a document with one error WHEN ValidationPanel renders THEN a red badge with '1' is visible
GIVEN a document with zero errors WHEN ValidationPanel renders THEN a green 'Valid' indicator is visible

title: Add JSON save/load to toolbar (native file dialogs)
preconditions: diagram_tool is a dioxus::desktop app (has access to native OS APIs via std::fs and std::process)
postconditions: Toolbar gains 'Save' button that opens a native save-file dialog and writes DiagramDocument as pretty-printed JSON
Toolbar gains 'Open' button that opens a native open-file dialog and loads a DiagramDocument from JSON, replacing doc_signal
Current revision is preserved on load (or reset to Revision::INITIAL if the file has none)
Errors (file not found, parse failure) are displayed in a non-panicking status message in the toolbar — never crash
invariants: Save and Load are pure I/O side effects — they must not mutate any Signal during the async file I/O operation itself, only write to doc_signal after successful parse
The history stack is cleared on successful Load (user gets a fresh undo stack)
No WASM deps (no web_sys, no Blob, no js_sys) — use std::fs exclusively
implementation_notes: Dioxus desktop: use dioxus::desktop::use_window() to get the window handle, then call window.create_file_dialog() for native file picker. Alternatively use the rfd crate (Rusty File Dialog) which is the standard for Dioxus desktop
If rfd is used, add rfd = '0.14' to diagram_tool/Cargo.toml. rfd::FileDialog::new().add_filter('Seshat Diagram', &['json']).save_file() returns Option<PathBuf>
SAVE: spawn(async move { ... }) to avoid blocking the Dioxus event loop. Write with serde_json::to_writer_pretty
LOAD: spawn(async move { ... }). Read file, serde_json::from_reader, on success write to doc_signal and reset history_signal
Status message: add a Signal<Option<String>> for toolbar_message. Show it in toolbar for 3 seconds then clear via gloo_timers (already available in desktop via tokio::time::sleep)
test_plan: GIVEN a document with 3 nodes WHEN Save is invoked with a temp path THEN a valid JSON file is written and serde_json::from_str succeeds on the output
GIVEN a valid JSON file on disk WHEN Load is invoked THEN doc_signal contains the loaded document and history is empty
GIVEN a path to a file containing invalid JSON WHEN Load is invoked THEN doc_signal is unchanged and a toolbar error message appears
GIVEN a document WHEN saved and then loaded THEN the round-tripped document equals the original (all node positions, labels, edges preserved)
